description: This diagnosis refers to

Recurrent isolated sleep paralysis is a chronic condition characterized by repeated episodes of temporary inability to move or speak while falling asleep or upon awakening, often accompanied by vivid hallucinations.
A record indicating that the patient has previously sustained a traumatic brain injury, which may influence current neurological assessment.
Acute inflammation of the brain parenchyma caused by Neisseria meningitidis infection.
Postinfectious hypothyroidism is a delayed, often subacute, reduction in thyroid hormone production following an upper respiratory or other systemic infection.
A group of anemias caused by vitamin B12 deficiency due to malabsorption, dietary insufficiency, or other non-pernicious causes.
Transient bilateral retinal artery occlusion is a temporary, painless loss of vision in both eyes due to brief arterial occlusion, often resolving within minutes to hours.
Mild cognitive impairment of uncertain or unknown etiology is a subtle decline in memory or executive function that does not yet meet criteria for dementia and has no identified cause.
A bladder dysfunction caused by neuromuscular disorders not otherwise specified, leading to urinary retention or incontinence due to impaired detrusor or sphincter control.
A disorder characterized by impaired coordination of bladder muscle activity leading to urinary retention or incontinence without a known underlying cause.
A progressive, bilateral sensorineural hearing loss due to abnormal bone remodeling in the cochlea.
Bilateral transient visual loss is a brief, reversible loss of vision in both eyes, often lasting seconds to minutes, associated with transient ischemia or neurological events.
Sudden bilateral loss of vision, often due to central nervous system or ocular vascular events.
Sudden, brief loss of vision in the right eye that resolves within 24 hours, often painless and without other neurological deficits.
Transient, painless loss of vision in the left eye, often due to a brief ischemic event such as amaurosis fugax.
Transient visual loss, unspecified eye is a brief, temporary loss of vision in one eye that resolves spontaneously within minutes to hours.
Sudden, painless loss of vision in the right eye that occurs abruptly and is often accompanied by a curtain‑like shadow or complete blindness.
Sudden loss of vision in the left eye, often occurring within minutes to hours.
Nonexudative age‑related macular degeneration is a chronic, bilateral retinal disease characterized by drusen accumulation and gradual loss of central vision without exudation.
A bilateral proliferative retinal disease not caused by diabetes, characterized by neovascularization and potential vision loss due to retinal ischemia.
A tremor disorder that does not meet criteria for other specific tremor types, typically presenting with action or postural tremor of variable frequency and amplitude.
Acute seizures triggered by external causes that progress to status epilepticus but are not refractory to initial treatment.
A condition characterized by vertigo and imbalance due to dysfunction of both vestibular organs.
A degenerative joint disease characterized by cartilage breakdown and joint space narrowing in the hip, leading to pain and stiffness.
A chronic focal epilepsy syndrome characterized by complex partial seizures that are refractory to treatment and occur without status epilepticus.
